# Decisions

Every dated decision in this project, the newest identifier last. An ADR is never
edited after acceptance; a later one supersedes it.

The directory is short because the threshold is high: an ADR rejects a named
alternative, is cross-cutting and is expensive to reverse. A ruling that meets only the
first condition has an address in a normative document — `spec/design/conventions.md`
§ When a decision is an ADR says which.

**`Supersedes`** names the identifiers this decision overrides, including frozen domain
rules (`BR-14` — they resolve in the context document that owns them, under
`../contexts/`) — so "which of my inherited rules have been overridden" is one grep over
this column.

**`Aliases`** names earlier identifiers still cited from code and tests. They resolve
here or in `spec/invariants.md`, where the rule itself lives; they are never renamed,
because renaming would break the citations they are worth having for.
